title: Kosmos 2542 and Kosmos 2543 near USA 245
status: Development reconstruction; supported windows are narrower than the historical episode

windows.label: December 31 · three spacecraft
windows.chapterNarrative: A short reconstruction shows both Russian spacecraft relative to USA 245. It does not establish a measured close approach.
windows.note: All three spacecraft have nearby dated elements. USA 245's element is roughly 8–10 hours from this window; this is geometry, not a measured close approach.

windows.label: December 7 · after deployment
windows.chapterNarrative: Following its December 6 release from Kosmos 2542, the smaller spacecraft can be viewed alongside USA 245 using a nearby observer element.
windows.note: USA 245 has a nearby amateur-derived element. The Russian spacecraft have dated elements within the display gate, but Kosmos 2542's is over 12 hours away.

windows.label: December 8 · second observer window
windows.chapterNarrative: A second observer element supports a separate view of both Russian spacecraft and USA 245; the intervening gap is not reconstructed.
windows.note: The second December USA 245 element supports a short, separate reconstruction. No track is drawn across the gap from December 7.

windows.label: January 24 · Russian spacecraft only
windows.chapterNarrative: Dated elements show the Russian spacecraft after reported January maneuvers. USA 245 has no nearby element here, so its position and both USA 245 comparisons remain unavailable.
windows.note: USA 245 has no nearby local element. Only Kosmos 2542 and Kosmos 2543 are rendered; no B position or B-pair statistic is inferred.
